Did Kamala Harris hit a 13-year-old girl with a car and leave the scene in 2011?
No, that's not true: The "KBSF-TV" news station cited in the social media post does not exist in San Francisco and the website that posted the article was created two weeks before the post appeared.
The San Francisco Police Department told Lead Stories they had no records of such an incident and believed the claim had no merit.
The image used in the article is from a car crash that happened in 2018 and was published then by major news organizations.
> BREAKING: A 26-year-old woman from San Francisco, Alicia Brown, alleges that Kamala Harris was involved in a 2011 hit-and-run accident that left her unable to walk.

The 4:39-minute video opens with shaky footage of what appears to be a street in hilly San Francisco and the audio, "It happened on the evening of June 7, 2011." Eventually it shows a woman describing an accident and accusing Harris of driving the car that hit her.
This video was originally published in an article on the website kbsf-tv.com, but was deleted as of this writing.
In June 2011, Harris was the newly elected attorney general of California (archived here), with offices in San Francisco.
There are no credible reports (archived here) of Harris being involved in an accident in San Francisco in June 2011.
Lead Stories has reached out to the California Highway Patrol for comment on the claim and we will update the story when a response is received.
We also contacted the Harris campaign for comment.
